## Overview of the Three Options

In 2026, there are three options that dominate new projects: Clerk, Better Auth, and Auth.js v5.

**Clerk:** Clerk is a managed authentication service that provides pre-built UI components, and you hand off the auth state to Clerk's systems.

**Better Auth:** Better Auth is an open-source library that runs in your app, with authentication state living in your database, allowing you to write less code than managing auth yourself but keep full control of the data.

**Auth.js v5:** Auth.js v5 (formerly NextAuth.js) is the most established open-source option — battle-tested, 40+ provider adapters, and now fully compatible with the Next.js App Router after a significant rewrite.

## Feature Comparison

Auth.js has limited features with no built-in 2FA, passkeys, or RBAC. In contrast, Better Auth offers the most complete feature set with 2FA, passkeys, RBAC, impersonation, and more.

## Performance

Better Auth's auth checks are direct database queries with no external API call, typically completing in under 5ms in production.

Clerk overhauled its pricing in February 2026, moving the free tier from 10,000 to 50,000 monthly active users, with the Pro plan starting at $25/mo and adding $0.02 per MAU above 50,000. In contrast, Better Auth's core library is free and open-source (MIT license) forever.

## Recommendations

Pick Clerk if you're building B2B SaaS where organizations matter or need features like passkeys without writing them yourself; Pick Better Auth if you want open source with full data ownership; Pick Auth.js v5 if you need a specific OAuth provider or want the most community resources available.

## Recent Development

Based on the search results, here's what you need to know about the Next.js 16 change from middleware.ts to proxy.ts:

## Key Changes

With the release of Next.js 16, middleware.js / middleware.ts has been replaced by proxy.js / proxy.ts, and it represents a major shift in how Next.js handles routing, request interception, authentication, rewrites, and performance optimization.

## Purpose of the Change

The rename from middleware.ts to proxy.ts in Next.js 16 Beta is meant to clarify its role at the network boundary, focusing on request routing and proxying rather than traditional app-level middleware logic. The term "proxy" better reflects the role this file now plays — handling routing, edge requests, and network interactions rather than just middleware logic.

## File Location and Runtime

An important change is the file location: The old middleware.ts was in root or src/, but the new proxy.ts must be inside the App Router directory at app/proxy.ts. Additionally, proxy.ts runs on Node.js (by default), not the limited Edge Runtime.

## Scope Limitations

proxy.ts is strictly for Routing (Rewrites, Redirects, Headers) and NOT for Authentication. Authentication in Next.js 16 should be handled in Server Layout Guards — layout.tsx files that verify the session using React Server Components, moving security checks closer to the data layer instead of the network edge.

--- title: Next.js 16 description: Next.js 16 includes Cache Components, stable Turbopack, file system caching, React Compiler support, smarter routing, new caching APIs, and React 19.2 features. url: "https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16" docs_index: /docs/llms.txt publishedAt: October 21st 2025 authors: - Jimmy Lai - Josh Story - Sebastian Markbåge - Tim Neutkens --- Ahead of our upcoming [Next.js Conf 2025](https://nextjs.org/conf), Next.js 16 is now available. This release provides the latest improvements to Turbopack, caching, and the Next.js architecture. Since the previous beta release, we added several new features and improvements: - [**Cache Components**](/blog/next-16#cache-components): New model using Partial Pre-Rendering (PPR) and use cache for instant navigation. - [**Next.js Devtools MCP**](/blog/next-16#nextjs-devtools-mcp): Model Context Protocol integration for improved debugging and workflow. - [**Proxy**](/blog/next-16#proxyts-formerly-middlewarets): Middleware replaced by `proxy.ts` to clarify network boundary. - [**DX**](/blog/next-16#logging-improvements): Improved logging for builds and development requests. For reminder, those features were available since the previous beta release: - [**Turbopack (stable)**](#turbopack-stable): Default bundler for all apps with up to 5-10x faster Fast Refresh, and 2-5x faster builds - [**Turbopack File System Caching (beta)**](#turbopack-file-system-caching-beta): Even faster startup and compile times for the largest apps - [**React Compiler Support (stable)**](#react-compiler-support-stable): Built-in integration for automatic memoization - [**Build Adapters API (alpha)**](#build-adapters-api-alpha): Create custom adapters to modify the build process - [**Enhanced Routing**](#enhanced-routing-and-navigation): Optimized navigations and prefetching with layout deduplication and incremental prefetching - [**Improved Caching APIs**](#improved-caching-apis): New `updateTag()` and refined `revalidateTag()` - [**React 19.2**](#react-192-and-canary-features): View Transitions, `useEffectEvent()`, `` - [**Breaking Changes**](#breaking-changes-and-other-updates): Async params, `next/image` defaults, and more Upgrade to Next.js 16: ```bash filename="terminal" # Use the automated upgrade CLI npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest # ...or upgrade manually npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest # ...or start a new project npx create-next-app@latest ``` For cases where the codemod can't fully migrate your code, please read the [upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). ## New Features and Improvements ### Cache Components Cache Components are a new set of features designed to make caching in Next.js both more explicit, and more flexible. They center around the new `"use cache"` directive, which can be used to cache pages, components, and functions, and which leverages the compiler to automatically generate cache keys wherever it’s used. Unlike the implicit caching found in previous versions of the App Router, caching with Cache Components is entirely opt-in. All dynamic code in any page, layout, or API route is executed at request time by default, giving Next.js an out-of-the-box experience that’s better aligned with what developers expect from a full-stack application framework. Cache Components also complete the story of Partial Prerendering (PPR), which was first introduced in 2023. Prior to PPR, Next.js had to choose whether to render each URL statically or dynamically; there was no middle ground. PPR eliminated this dichotomy, and let developers opt portions of their static pages into dynamic rendering (via Suspense) without sacrificing the fast initial load of fully static pages. You can enable Cache Components in your `next.config.ts` file: ```ts filename="next.config.ts" const nextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, }; export default nextConfig; ``` We will be sharing more about Cache Components and how to use them at [Next.js Conf 2025](https://nextjs.org/conf) on October 22nd, and we will be sharing more content in our blog and documentation in the coming weeks. > **Note:** as previously announced in the beta release, the previous experimental `experimental.ppr` flag and configuration options have been removed in favor of the Cache Components configuration. Learn more in the documentation [here](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). ### Next.js Devtools MCP Next.js 16 introduces **Next.js DevTools MCP**, a Model Context Protocol integration for AI-assisted debugging with contextual insight into your application. The Next.js DevTools MCP provides AI agents with: - **Next.js knowledge**: Routing, caching, and rendering behavior - **Unified logs**: Browser and server logs without switching contexts - **Automatic error access**: Detailed stack traces without manual copying - **Page awareness**: Contextual understanding of the active route This enables AI agents to diagnose issues, explain behavior, and suggest fixes directly within your development workflow. Learn more in the documentation [here](/docs/app/guides/mcp). ### `proxy.ts` (formerly `middleware.ts`) `proxy.ts` replaces `middleware.ts` and makes the app’s network boundary explicit. `proxy.ts` runs on the Node.js runtime. - **What to do**: Rename `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts` and rename the exported function to `proxy`. Logic stays the same. - **Why**: Clearer naming and a single, predictable runtime for request interception. ```ts filename="proxy.ts" export default function proxy(request: NextRequest) { return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url)); } ``` > **Note:** The `middleware.ts` file is still available for Edge runtime use cases, but it is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. ## Proxy

> **Good to know**: Starting with Next.js 16, Middleware is now called Proxy to better reflect its purpose. The functionality remains the same.

Proxy allows you to run code before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

### Use cases

Some common scenarios where Proxy is effective include:

* Modifying headers for all pages or a subset of pages
* Rewriting to different pages based on A/B tests or experiments
* Programmatic redirects based on incoming request properties

For simple redirects, consider using the [`redirects`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/redirects) configuration in `next.config.ts` first. Proxy should be used when you need access to request data or more complex logic.

Proxy is *not* intended for slow data fetching. While Proxy can be helpful for [optimistic checks](/docs/app/guides/authentication#optimistic-checks-with-proxy-optional) such as permission-based redirects, it should not be used as a full session management or authorization solution.

Using fetch with `options.cache`, `options.next.revalidate`, or `options.next.tags`, has no effect in Proxy.

### Convention

Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.

> **Note**: While only one `proxy.ts` file is supported per project, you can still organize your proxy logic into modules. Break out proxy functionalities into separate `.ts` or `.js` files and import them into your main `proxy.ts` file. This allows for cleaner management of route-specific proxy, aggregated in the `proxy.ts` for centralized control. By enforcing a single proxy file, it simplifies configuration, prevents potential conflicts, and optimizes performance by avoiding multiple proxy layers.

### Example

You can export your proxy function as either a default export or a named `proxy` export:

```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

// Alternatively, you can use a default export:
// export default function proxy(request: NextRequest) { ... }

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

// Alternatively, you can use a default export:
// export default function proxy(request) { ... }

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

The `matcher` config allows you to filter Proxy to run on specific paths. See the [Matcher](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#matcher) documentation for more details on path matching.

Read more about [using `proxy`](/docs/app/guides/backend-for-frontend#proxy), or refer to the `proxy` [API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).

content.content:
# Better Auth CLI for Kysely/SQLite

## Commands

**Generate schema:**
```bash
npx auth@latest generate --adapter kysely
```

**Apply migration:**
```bash
npx auth@latest migrate
```

## Config File

Create `auth.ts` (or `better-auth.config.ts`) in your project root, `./lib`, or `./utils`:

```typescript
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import { sqlite } from "better-auth/adapters/sqlite";
import Database from "better-sqlite3";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  database: new sqlite("auth.db"),
  emailAndPassword: { enabled: true },
  socialProviders: { google: { clientId: "", clientSecret: "" } }
});
```

## Tables Created

With email/password + Google provider (default plugins only), the schema generates these core tables:

- `user` (stores user profiles)
- `account` (OAuth provider linkage)
- `session` (authentication sessions)
- `verification` (email verification tokens)
- `passkey` (optional, for passwordless auth)

The exact table structure depends on your database dialect. Run the `generate` command to see the specific SQL schema for your setup.

Всё готово и проверено (build, lint, dev и prod-режим — сквозной прогон через curl: регистрация, логин, доступ к /dashboard, выход, редиректы). Собираю итог.

## Что выбрал и почему

Сравнил три варианта (Clerk, Auth.js v5, Better Auth) — [сравнение 2026](https://blog.logrocket.com/best-auth-library-nextjs-2026/), [ещё одно](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk), [и это](https://blog.codercops.com/blog/nextjs-auth-comparison-clerk-better-auth-2026). Взял **[Better Auth](https://www.better-auth.com/)**: open-source, MIT, данные у вас в БД, а не в чужом сервисе, из коробки есть email+password и Google OAuth, нативно ложится на App Router. Clerk — управляемый сервис (аккаунт, hosted UI, платный тариф) — избыточен для этого проекта. Auth.js v5 беднее фичами. Замечание в сторону: 7 июля 2026 Vercel купил команду Better Auth — сигнал, что библиотека не заброшена.

## Что сделано

- **`src/lib/auth.ts`** — сервер Better Auth: email/password + условно Google (включается только если заданы `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`, иначе плейсхолдеры не ломают приложение), БД — SQLite-файл `notely.db` (гитигнорится).
- **`src/lib/users.ts`** — переписан: `listUsers/getUser/getCurrentUser` теперь читают реальную таблицу `user` вместо хардкод-массива. Сигнатуры не поменялись, dashboard/page.tsx трогать не пришлось.
- **`/api/auth/[...all]`** — роут-хендлер Better Auth.
- **`src/proxy.ts`** — в Next 16 middleware переименован в proxy; оптимистичный редирект `/dashboard/*` → `/sign-in` по наличию cookie.
- **`src/app/dashboard/layout.tsx`** — жёсткая проверка сессии на сервере (по рекомендации самого Next 16 — proxy только для роутинга, реальная авторизация в layout-гвардах).
- **`/sign-in`, `/sign-up`** — формы email+password и кнопка «Continue with Google».
- Шапка сайта (`layout.tsx`) — ссылки Sign in/Sign up или Dashboard/Sign out в зависимости от сессии.
